tracks.title: Midnight Animal
tracks.plain_lyrics:
Another recovered bootleg from the Dream Machine Tour cycle (1986–87).

Unlike most dates in this era — typically branded and distributed by Orion — this feed carried AWN’s imprint throughout.
In-universe, AWN rarely attached their name to concert simulations, preferring the posture of “serious journalism.” When they did, it was generally to reinforce cultural unity and national spectacle.

That sponsorship frames the artifact: AWN’s stamp positions the track as sanctioned adrenaline rather than threat, turning a volatile performance into a safe, mass-audience spectacle.

On Broadcast Context: By the mid-80s, Live-Fidelity performance simulations had largely replaced physical touring.
Nova’s “crowds” were programmatic loops; the “tour” was a schedule of studio transmissions over the WorldNet.
This master reflects that grammar—crisp camera blocking, repeatable banter beats, and Orion-style overlays.

Persistent AWN Logo: The AWN corner bug is present for almost the entire runtime — unusual for culture slots, where AWN typically appears as bumpers/IDs before and after.
A full-runtime mark implies news-division custodianship or a compliance-mode rebroadcast, asserting ownership over the signal rather than merely “presenting” it.

Listing Marked “Edited”: The broadcast was cataloged as Edited, almost certainly indicating a post-event compliance pass: trims to between-song patter, replacement of crowd beds, and minor continuity repairs.
The cut also preserves the AWN retitle across slates.

One short drop-frame patch over Camera-2 suggests an anomaly seam that was sanded down for syndication.
